result.killer: No single killer was found. Risks: the decree is still pending (180-day phase-in after it is published), the free state tools (RIHP and the Mintur online registry), and Anfy, a PMS sold in Uruguay to this segment that is already positioned around Ley 20.352.
result.reason: Not refuted, but the duty doesn't bite yet. As of 13 Sep 2026 the decree under Ley 20.352 was still under review at Interior, MEF and MVOT. Hosts then get 180 days, so nothing is enforceable before about mid-2027. Mintur's registry will be free and online. Hotels already report guests through the Interior Ministry's free RIHP (Decreto 390/2013, 12-hour deadline), the likely channel for rentals too. No API spec was found. Anfy (anfy.app), a PMS and channel manager sold in Uruguay to cabins, apartments and hostels, already writes about this law. It stores guest data, so it could add the report cheaply. The market is mostly seasonal hosts (Punta del Este). Unsettled: final decree text, how guest reports are filed, number of hosts.

result.killer: None found. Partial substitutes: Crowe Uruguay's done-for-you PLAFT service, SENACLAFT's free sector guides with forms (form content unverified, PDF unreadable), the LUC simplification for electronic payments, and generic AML screening APIs such as Didit.
result.reason: Eight Spanish-language searches found no Uruguay-specific PLAFT SaaS for non-financial obliged subjects. The only things close to it are Crowe's done-for-you due-diligence reports for estate agents and auctioneers, manuals from law firms (Ferrere, RSM) and generic screening APIs (Didit). None of these kills the idea. It is weakened in three ways. SENACLAFT publishes free sector guides with standard forms; the guide text quotes an observations box on "the forms", but I could not open the PDF. Under Ley 19.889 (LUC), due diligence can be simplified when payment is electronic. And Uruguay is a small market whose size I could not find. Ley 20.469 added new subjects: Res. 54/2026 opened their registration (deadline 10/07/2026) and Res. 61/2026 set a new sanctions scale. These give fresh triggers, but SENACLAFT recorded only 50 sanctions in 2023, so enforcement is light.

coverage.category: 1. Household employers: domestic workers, live-in carers, nannies

coverage.category: 3. Second-hand dealers and pawnbrokers
coverage.found: No Uruguayan pawn or second-hand register found. The SENACLAFT page lists only intermediaries in antiques, art, metals and precious stones (see candidate C01). Pawn shops, second-hand dealers and jewellers are not named on the page I read (unverified whether covered).

coverage.category: 4. Gold and jewellery buyers
coverage.found: Intermediaries in precious metals and stones are non-financial obliged parties under art. 13 Ley 19.574: they must register with SENACLAFT, report suspicious transactions (ROS) to the UIAF and keep records 5 years. Ley 20.469 (19 Mar 2026) and SENACLAFT Res. 061/2026 (stricter sanctions) are new. See C01.

coverage.category: 5. Used car parts and vehicle dismantlers
coverage.found: No Uruguayan dismantler register or rule found; search returned only Argentine Ley 25.761 and 2025 decrees. Nothing new.

coverage.category: 6. Livestock traders, markets and animal transport
coverage.found: DICOSE annual sworn declaration runs 1-31 July (Res. 975/026 for 2026); electronic filing is mandatory for commercial or intermediary DICOSE numbers, dairies, feedlots and others. SNIG is the free state platform; the animal-movement guide rules were not confirmed. See C10 (weak).

coverage.category: 7. Small abattoirs and butchers
coverage.found: Nothing new beyond K05 (butcher monthly INAC declaration). Not re-checked.

coverage.category: 8. Beekeepers
coverage.found: Annual hive declaration (RNPC/SINATPA) is mandatory. New: MGAP DGSG Res. 025/2026 (15 Jan 2026) requires an electronic field notebook for every apiary, complete before the annual declaration, a condition for export eligibility, and takes effect 12 months after publication. MGAP supplies the system free via gub.uy ID. About 2,800 producers and 600k hives. See C02.

coverage.category: 9. Veterinary practices and veterinary medicine sellers
coverage.found: Shops must be registered with DILAVE/MGAP, have a veterinary technical lead, pay an annual fee, and keep prescriptions for 2 years with the DICOSE number for production animals (Res. DGSG 193/015). Res. 1169/016 requires electronic recording of tick-killer and fly-killer stock movements on the SNIG platform. No electronic prescription rule found. See C04.

coverage.category: 10. Well drillers and water abstraction
coverage.found: Drilling firms need a DINAGUA licence (Codigo de Aguas art. 45, Decreto 86/004), valid up to 5 years, with a geologist as responsible technician. Water-use rights and study permits go through DINAGUA's online process. Small niche. See C05.

coverage.category: 11. Septic, sanitation and waste haulers
coverage.found: Barometrica (septic truck) firms are licensed by each departmental government (Canelones: 24 UR plus 3 UR per vehicle, valid 3 years; Montevideo has dumping-site rules). Decreto 213/2025 (Ley 19.829, construction waste) obliges haulers to use the traceability system, close to K01. See C06. No national barometrica traceability found.

coverage.category: 12. Lift, boiler and pressure-equipment owners and inspectors
coverage.found: Lifts: nothing new beyond K06. Boilers: URSEA regulates steam generators (above 0.5 barg). It keeps a register of owners and of 'agentes vinculados', LATU carries out annual inspections and an inspection fee applies, and a professional makes an annual sworn declaration of tests. The regulation was approved by Res. 101/026 (17 Mar 2026; unverified). Pressure vessels other than boilers not found. See C03.

coverage.category: 13. Small water systems
coverage.found: URSEA Res. 120/2018 requires Water Safety Plans from providers, and Res. 259/026 (Jul 2026) amends the water-quality regulation annex. Rural MEVIR systems that have not been handed to OSE are 'orphans' (academic source). No registration duty found for small private systems.

coverage.category: 14. Pesticide and fertiliser dealers and applicators
coverage.found: MGAP Res. 317/2022: every pesticide distributor must be registered with DGSA and, from 1 Jan 2023, employ at least one holder of a safe-use pesticide carnet; penalties include suspension up to 180 days and closure. Res. 959/022 created the Registro Unico de Operadores for self-applicators (terrestrial rigs of 1,000 litres or more, and aerial). Spray-log case is K04. An ACA 2026 document on a 'registro responsable de plaguicidas' could not be read (PDF). See C07.

coverage.category: 15. Labour contractors and recruitment agencies
coverage.found: Staffing and placement agencies must hold a DINAE/MTSS licence, apply online via gub.uy, be current with DGI, BPS and BSE, and file the Planilla de Trabajo Unificada. Ley 18.099 and 18.251 make user firms jointly liable for contractors' labour and social-security debts. See C08.

coverage.category: 16. Cemeteries, burial societies and funeral services
coverage.found: No national funeral or cemetery rule from 2025-26 found. Regulation is departmental, for example Canelones Ordenanza de Necropolis 95/15 and an online portal where private cemetery parks file cremations and transfers and pay a per-cremation fee. Few operators. Weak, see C09.

coverage.category: 17. Community and religious bodies: associations, charities, halal and kosher supervision
coverage.found: Associations and foundations must report their governing-body members as beneficial owners to the BCU (Ley 19.484, Decreto 166/017), by notarised sworn form, and update on change. Associations under UI 4,000,000 income and UI 2,500,000 assets are exempt (a 2019 decree, per a law-firm note). MEC suspended legal personality of bodies that did not register in the national census. Halal and kosher supervision not searched. See C11.

coverage.category: 18. Transport operators: minibus, taxi, moto-taxi, small trucking and bus fleets
coverage.found: Taxi, remise and school-transport vehicle registration is by the departmental government (Montevideo trámite updated Jan 2025); Res. 16/022 DNT covers school transport. MTSS publishes taxi-driver viatico adjustments (Jul 2026). Canelones allowed app-based permits in Feb 2026. No national recurring reporting duty found. Weak, see C12.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: No dedicated search. Budget used on categories with clearer registers. Money changers are BCU-supervised (not verified here).

coverage.category: 20. Small licensed premises with inspections: tattoo studios, driving schools, childminders and nurseries, small food producers, hunting outfitters
coverage.found: Only nurseries and driving schools searched. Private early-childhood centres: Ley 18.437 art. 97-101 and Decreto 268/014; the authority changed from 1 Jan 2021 (which body now registers them is unverified). Driving schools: Ley 16.585, each departmental government keeps a register. Tattoo studios, hunting outfitters and small food producers not searched. See C13.

coverage.category: 19. Market traders, street vendors, money changers
coverage.found: Money changers: need prior BCU authorisation (Decreto 680/1991); BCU supervises, can require records and periodic reports; they file suspicious-transaction reports (ROS) to the BCU's UIAF (Ley 19.574). BCU fined Cambio Fenix and Cambio Brimar about US$100k in June 2024 for failing their AML manual. The BCU page lists about 18+ small SA entities (list cut off, count unverified; the BCU page returned 503 on fetch). Only about 13-20 ROS a year came from casas de cambio in 2020-21, so the market is tiny. No local AML software for casas de cambio found (one search, weak signal). Street/fair vendors: Montevideo neighbourhood food fairs (about 164 fairs in 2020) are run through MEF/UDECO. A feriante status needs a long document set (health card, DGI, BPS certificate, food handler card, LATU scale verification, bromatology licence) and a ground-fee (tasa de piso) paid to the Intendencia. Ambulant vendors without a fixed stand need no prior permit. Fair rules are administrative and free to apply, and no fair-software vendors found. See candidates C1 and C2. Unchecked: current exact count of casas de cambio, BCU AML norm text (Recopilacion de Normas), whether the 2026 crypto/virtual-asset regime applies to casas de cambio, Intendencia fee amounts.

Honey: Decreto 371/2013 makes traceability mandatory (registration with DIGEGRA, annual sworn declaration online, SINATPA web system); Decreto 29/2006 requires licensed extraction rooms; exporters register with MGAP-DGSG and get DILAVE zoosanitary certificates per lot, sent 48 working hours before shipment. Timber: only EUDR items (first pilot wood-chip and sawn-timber exports done under the state georeferencing process, already covered by K07). Organic: Decreto 557/008 and Decreto 175/022 (labelling), with export audited by international certifiers and small farmers using a participatory guarantee scheme; no small-exporter register found. All main filings run through free state portals (VUCE, SINATPA, DILAVE electronic certification). See candidates C3 to C5. Unchecked: current VUCE/DINARA fees, number of small fish plants, number of honey exporters and acopios, whether SINATPA/DILAVE systems have cost-free tools for bulk batch records.

result.competitor: I found no private AML software for Uruguayan non-financial obligated parties in Spanish-language searches. SENACLAFT publishes free due-diligence forms and guides by sector, including one for this sector, plus training. Its communiqué of 04 Sep 2026 says obligated parties may outsource due diligence to professionals or firms, but SENACLAFT does not register or approve them, which suggests a consulting market (Ferrere, RSM and others). Generic regional AML tools were not checked.
result.duty: Ley 19.574 Art. 13 lit. F, as reworded by Ley 20.469 (19/03/2026, published 10/04/2026), covers natural and legal persons who broker sales of antiques, art, metals and precious stones. They must register with SENACLAFT, run a written risk assessment and report suspicious operations to the UIAF. Customer due diligence applies to operations of USD 15,000 or more, including linked operations within a calendar year (Decreto 379/018 art. 64). Records are kept 5 years. Fines run from 1,000 to 20,000,000 UI. Res. 061/2026 replaces Res. 016/2022 and makes unreported operations and failure to register grave infractions (per secondary sources RSM and abogados.com.ar; I did not open the official text). Retail jewellers and pawn shops are not named in Art. 13.
result.market: Not found. I found no SENACLAFT statistics on registered dealers in this sector. It is probably a small niche in Uruguay (likely a few hundred businesses, unverified), and many fall below the USD 15,000 due-diligence threshold.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. IMPO's consolidated Ley 19.574 Art. 13, as reworded by Ley 20.469 (19 Mar 2026), names people who broker sales of antiques, art, metals and precious stones. Fines run from 1,000 to 20M UI. Res. 061/2026 makes failing to register or to report a grave infraction. But customer checks apply only to deals of USD 15,000 or more (Decreto 379/018 art. 64), so tiny dealers rarely trigger them. Whether retail jewellers and pawn shops are covered is unclear, since the law names brokers. I found no AML software for these dealers. SENACLAFT's free forms, guides and training, plus consulting firms, cover most needs. I found no count of registered dealers; Uruguay's segment is likely a few hundred. Low pay and little frequent work.

result.competitor: State tools: Mintur's registry will be free and online (draft decree). The Interior Ministry already runs the RIHP (Decreto 390/2013), which the ministry administers and supports through its Division de Sistemas de Informacion. It is the likely channel for guest reports from short-term rentals, which would make that part free. I found no public API spec. Products: I found no Uruguay-specific host-compliance tool and no PMS advertising RIHP or Ley 20.352 compliance. Spanish tools such as Chekin cover Spain's SES.HOSPEDAJES, not Uruguay. Not checked: whether international PMS or channel managers have added Uruguay support.
result.duty: Ley 20.352 (in force, 2024). Art. 3: sworn declaration in the Mintur Registro de Operadores Turisticos, with the registration number in every offer. Art. 4: keep the registry up to date and accept inspections under Ley 19.253. Report the number of guests and days to Mintur each year or on request. Report each guest's name, ID and country of origin to the Interior Ministry "periodicamente" (no interval set), keep copies of IDs for 5 years, and get guests' informed consent. The law has no sanctions article. Art. 6 says the Executive will issue regulations, with no deadline. As of 2 Jul 2026 (Ambito) the decree was still unissued, with the draft under review by Interior, MEF and MVOT. I found no later publication but did not check IMPO directly after that date. Draft (Mintur, 24 Nov 2025): covers stays up to 120 days, online registration on the Mintur site, platforms may only list registered units, 180 days to adapt, gradual rollout. Separately, Decreto 390/2013 already makes hotels, pensiones, alojamientos, chacras turisticas and casas de inquilinato enter guests in the Interior Ministry's RIHP within 12 hours.
result.market: Not reached. I found no current count of hosts or listings. The only figure was about 4,300 Airbnb listings in 2016 (AFP, cited by search results), which is too old to use. The Mintur registry is not yet operational for these rentals. Not counted: Mintur registered operators, AirDNA data, and the number of hotels already in the RIHP.
result.reason: The law exists but the duty is not yet operational. Ley 20.352 Art. 3-4 requires registry, annual Mintur report and periodic guest reporting to Interior, but sets no frequency, no sanctions and no regulation deadline. On 2 Jul 2026 the decree was still unissued, and I found nothing published since. Once issued, hosts get 180 days. Mintur's registry will be free and online. Guest reporting will likely use the Interior Ministry's existing free RIHP, where hotels already enter guests within 12 hours (Decreto 390/2013), so a free state tool may cover the core job. No Uruguay-specific vendor was found. Host count is unknown. The draft decree covers stays up to 120 days. Copying guests' IDs needs their consent (URCDP dictamen 16/2023). Timing, format and whether anyone will pay are all uncertain.

result.competitor: No Uruguay-specific PLAFT SaaS for non-financial subjects turned up in 5 local-language searches. Existing options: Crowe Uruguay sells done-for-you PLAFT due-diligence reports for estate agents, auctioneers and notaries (delivered within 72 working hours); law firms and consultancies (Ferrere, RSM, PwC) sell manuals and advice; the UIAF/BCU publishes free control lists (PEPs, UN list, non-cooperating countries) but no workflow tool. Regional vendors from Argentina, Chile and Colombia were not seen targeting Uruguay; this was not exhaustively checked.
result.duty: Ley 19.574 art. 13 (as amended by Ley 20.469, promulgated 19/03/2026 and published 10/04/2026) and Decreto 379/018 apply to real estate agencies, developers, builders, auctioneers, and to accountants and lawyers on listed operations. From Res. 54/2026 (12/05/2026) they also cover non-financial trustees and providers of administration, accounting or data services to clients abroad. These subjects must register with SENACLAFT, appoint a compliance officer, keep a risk matrix, assess each client and operation in writing (low, medium or high risk), run due diligence, find source of funds and beneficial owners, train staff, report unusual operations to the UIAF and keep records for 5 years. Ley 20.469 cuts the cash threshold to UI 200,000 (or 5% of the operation, capped at UI 450,000) and requires updated matrices and manuals, but its regulation is still pending. Res. 061/2026 replaces Res. 016/2022 and makes failure to register, update data or perform due diligence, and failure to identify beneficial owners, serious infringements. The frequency is per transaction plus continuous upkeep. No fixed periodic filing was found.
result.market: No count found. No public statistic gives the number of registered non-financial subjects (checked SENACLAFT news and law-firm notes). As a proxy, the non-financial sector filed only 107 suspicious-activity reports in 2025, against 973 from the financial sector (Presidencia, citing the UIAF annual report). The buyer pool probably runs to a few thousand real estate firms, builders, auctioneers, accountants and corporate-service providers in a country of about 3.5M people. This is an estimate, not verified.
result.reason: The duty is real and in force. Ley 19.574 art. 13 and Decreto 379/018 require subjects to register with SENACLAFT, appoint a compliance officer, keep a risk matrix, write a risk analysis per client and operation, run due diligence and keep records for 5 years. Ley 20.469 (published 10/04/2026) and Res. 54/2026 added new subjects. Res. 061/2026 treats non-registration and missing due diligence as serious infringements. I found no software built for Uruguayan non-financial subjects, only consultancy services (Crowe's per-client PLAFT reports) and the free UIAF control lists. Repeat use comes from per-transaction due diligence, but it is event-driven, not a periodic filing. The market is small and uncounted. Only 107 non-financial suspicious-activity reports in 2025 suggests weak enforcement. Rules for Ley 20.469 are still pending.

The duty is real. URSEA Res. 101/026 (17/03/26) approves the current steam-generator regulation, which covers units with PMTA above 0.5 barg. Owners and a designated professional must be registered, and the professional files an annual sworn declaration of tests online with reports attached. Otherwise a LATU annual inspection is done and a fee paid. Penalties are URSEA administrative sanctions. I searched once for software and found none, but this is a thin check, not proof of absence. Weak points: the owner base is small and industrial, probably a few thousand units at most (no count found), the work is a professional's filing on free gub.uy trámites, and the pain is low. The 2026 deadline changes were not checked.

Duty is real: Res. MGAP 1169/016 (Vigía) requires establishments that sell veterinary products to record tick-killer and fly-killer stock in and out electronically on the state SNIG platform or app. The MGAP plan says a vet prescription is required for antibiotics, and Res. DGSG 193/015 exists. I did not confirm the 2-year retention, the DICOSE link, penalties, or whether later changes apply. The state portal and app already do the core job free, so the opening is only a stock-system integration. I did not find a shop count or any vendor product. Competition and market size are unchecked. The buyer base is probably small and the pain low.

result.competitor: None found for Uruguay. Spanish ERP for phytosanitary trade and Argentine tools exist but are not adapted to Uruguayan rules.
result.duty: DGSA Res. 317/022: RUO registration of the shop, at least one carnet holder on staff, and a purchase-sale book for Ia/Ib/atrazina products.
result.market: Not found. No register count located. Likely a few hundred shops, which is an unverified guess.
result.reason: The duty is real. DGSA Res. 317/022 bars primary distributors from selling to retailers without RUO registration (from 1 Jun 2022). A trade-press note adds that each shop needs a safe-use carnet holder (valid 4 years) from 1 Jan 2023. The same note lists penalties up to 180-day suspension and closure; I did not find these in the official text. The MGAP also checks the purchase-sale book for category Ia/Ib products and atrazina, plus web prescriptions. That is the only recurring element, and it is narrow. I found no local software for this niche, but I did not search local ERP vendors exhaustively. The market is small and I found no count of shops. Both PDFs (ACA 2026, MGAP dealer course) were unreadable, so any 2026 change is unchecked. Mostly one-off paperwork, so willingness to pay is low.

result.duty: Ley 18.099/18.251: the principal firm may demand compliance documents (art. 4) and is subsidiarily liable if it does so, otherwise jointly liable. No fixed frequency found.
result.market: Not quantified. No register count found.
result.reason: The duty is real (Ley 18.099 and 18.251). It is a right to information, not a mandatory filing. Art. 4 documents are the nominal payroll history plus BPS payment receipt, a BPS clearance certificate, a BSE certificate, and the payroll roster, salary receipts and collective agreement. Checking is the way to limit liability to subsidiary, but the law sets no frequency and no direct fine. Case law only says the control must be "periódico y efectivo". Competition exists: PwC Uruguay sells a supplier-control platform, and OSE tendered for outsourced contractor control. The market is hard to size, and buyers are mostly mid-size or large firms, with accountants and lawyers as the incumbents. Pain is moderate and willingness to pay from small firms is weak. I did not verify the DINAE licence side or buyer counts.

The duty is real. Ley 19.484 and Decreto 166/017, amended by Decreto 256/019 and 272/2022, require civil associations to file a notarised sworn declaration (Formulario B) with the BCU listing board members. Associations are exempt only if income is under UI 4M and assets under UI 2.5M, both at year-end. Changes must be reported within 30 days (90 days for non-residents); this comes from older sources. Penalties include fines and a suspended DGI certificate. No annual cycle was found, so it is mostly one-off plus update on change. No software competitor turned up, but a notary signature is required, and small buyers are scattered and low-paying. The market count and MEC census claim were not checked.

The duty is real. Decreto 260/007 requires an annual sworn declaration, or a no-scope declaration. It covers brand owners, importers, contract packagers and packaging makers. The 2026 deadline was 6 April, because 30 March fell on a non-business day. The gub.uy page lists no penalties or fees. Filing is an online gub.uy procedure plus a signed paper, and the Ministry's Mesa de Entrada accepts it in person. The state portal already does the filing, so software would only add data prep. No dedicated software competitor turned up, but I searched only briefly. Plan Vale (Cámara de Industrias) handles adhesion for 2,500+ firms. Annual frequency, a free state channel and likely accountant or CIU help limit willingness to pay. Market size was not verified beyond the 2,500 figure.
